explanation: Maintain parallel value and prefix-maximum stacks of equal depth. Every Push stores both the item and max(item,previous maximum), even when the maximum is unchanged. Pop removes one entry from each; GetMax peeks at the maximum stack.
correctness: At each depth the maximum stack stores the maximum of the matching value prefix. Pushing extends that invariant; removing the top entries restores the invariant for the shorter prefix. Repeated maxima persist in separate snapshots, so popping one occurrence cannot erase the remaining maximum.
walkthrough: Push 5: values=[5], maxima=[5]. Push 9: values=[5,9], maxima=[5,9]. GetMax returns 9. Pop removes one entry from both stacks and returns 9; GetMax now returns 5. If the second push had been 4, maxima would instead be [5,5], because every depth gets a snapshot. JSON supplies [operationNames,argumentLists] for one fresh MaxStack. Push displays null; Pop/GetMax display integer results or {"error":"empty"}.
edgeCases: After pushing 8 twice and popping once, GetMax still returns 8. Empty Pop/GetMax raise an exception normalized to {"error":"empty"}.
timeComplexity: O(1) per operation under the stack push/pop cost model (amortized for dynamically grown arrays): only a constant number of stack operations occur.
spaceComplexity: O(s) persistent space for s live entries, including their stored maximum information.
